entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 8 Ho 8:1-14 . Prophecy of the Irruption of the Assyrians, in Punishment for Israel's Apostasy, Idolatry, and Setting Up of Kings without God's Sanction. In Ho 8:14 , Judah is said to multiply fenced cities; and in Ho 8:7-9 , Israel, to its great hurt, is said to have gone up to Assyria for help. This answers best to the reign of Menahem. For it was then that Uzziah of Judah, his contemporary, built fenced cities ( 2Ch 26:6 , 9, 10 ). Then also Israel turned to Assyria and had to pay for their sinful folly a thousand talents of silver ( 2Ki 15:19 ) [Maurer]. 1. Set the trumpet, &c.-- to give warning of the approach of the enemy: "To thy palate (that is, 'mouth,' Job 31:30 , Margin) the trumpet"; the abruptness of expression indicates the suddenness of the attack. So Ho 5:8 . as ... eagle-- the Assyrian ( De 28:49 ; Jr 48:40 ; Ha 1:8 ). against ... house of ... Lord-- not the temple, but Israel viewed as the family of God ( Ho 9:15 ; Nu 12:7 ; Zec 9:8 ; He 3:2 ; 1Ti 3:15 ; 1Pe 4:17 ).

My God, we know thee--</hi>the singular, "My," is used distributively, each one so addressing God. They, in their hour of need, plead their knowledge of God as the covenant-people, while in their acts they acknowledge Him not (compare <reference osisRef="Matt.7.21">Mt 7:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.7.22">22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Titus.1.16">Tit 1:16</reference>; also <reference osisRef="Isa.29.13">Is 29:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.7.4">Jr 7:4</reference>). The Hebrew joins "Israel," not as English Version, with "shall cry," but "We, Israel, know thee"; God denies the claim thus urged on the ground of their descent from Israel. <div eID="gen22541" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_plain: 4. kings ... not by me-- not with My sanction ( 1Ki 11:31 ; 12:20 ). Israel set up Jeroboam and his successors, whereas God had appointed the house of David as the rightful kings of the whole nation. I knew it not-- I approved it not ( Psa 1:6 ). of ... gold ... idols-- ( Ho 2:8 ; 13:2 ). that they may be cut off-- that is, though warned of the consequences of idolatry, as it were with open eyes they rushed on their own destruction. So Jr 27:10 , 15 ; 44:8 .

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12344"/><div sID="gen22552" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12344"/><hi type="bold">7. sown ... reap--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Prov.22.8">Pr 22:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.6.7">Ga 6:7</reference>). "Sow ... wind," that is, to make the vain show of worship, while faith and obedience are wanting [Calvin]. Rather, to offer senseless supplications to the calves for good harvests (compare <reference osisRef="Hos.2.8">Ho 2:8</reference>); the result being that God will make them "reap no stalk," that is, "standing corn." Also, the phraseology proverbially means that all their undertakings shall be profitless (<reference osisRef="Prov.11.29">Pr 11:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.5.16">Ec 5:16</reference>).<div eID="gen22552" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22553" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the bud--</hi>or, "growth."<div eID="gen22553" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22554" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">strangers--</hi>foreigners (<reference osisRef="Hos.7.9">Ho 7:9</reference>). <div eID="gen22554" type="x-p"/>

Also, the phraseology proverbially means that all their undertakings shall be profitless ( Pr 11:29 ; Ec 5:16 ). the bud-- or, "growth." strangers-- foreigners ( Ho 7:9 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12346"/><div sID="gen22556" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12346"/><hi type="bold">9. gone ... to Assyria--</hi>referring to Menahem's application for Pul's aid in establishing him on the throne (compare <reference osisRef="Hos.5.13">Ho 5:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.7.11">7:11</reference>). Menahem's name is read in the inscriptions in the southwest palace of Nimrod, as a tributary to the Assyrian king in his eighth year. The dynasty of Pul, or Phalluka, was supplanted at Nineveh by that of Tiglath-pileser, about 768 (or 760) B.C. Semiramis seems to have been Pul's wife, and to have withdrawn to Babylon in 768; and her son, Nabonassar, succeeding after a period of confusion, originated "the era of Nabonassar," 747 B.C. [G. V. Smith]. Usually foreigners coming to Israel's land were said to "go up"; here it is the reverse, to intimate Israel's sunken state, and Assyria's superiority.<div eID="gen22556" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22557" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wild ass--</hi>a figure of Israel's headstrong perversity in following her own bent (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.24">Jr 2:24</reference>).<div eID="gen22557" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22558" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">alone by himself--</hi>characteristic of Israel in all ages: "lo, the people shall dwell alone" (<reference osisRef="Num.23.9">Nu 23:9</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Job.39.5-Job.39.8">Job 39:5-8</reference>).<div eID="gen22558" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22559" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hired lovers--</hi>reversing the ordinary way, namely, that lovers should hire her (<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.33">Eze 16:33</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.34">34</reference>). <div eID="gen22559" type="x-p"/>

entries.reader_content_plain: 12. great things of ... law-- ( De 4:6 , 8 ; Psa 19:8 ; 119:18 , 72 ; 147:19 , 20 ). Maurer not so well translates, "the many things of My law." my law-- as opposed to their inventions. This reference of Hosea to the Pentateuch alone is against the theory that some earlier written prophecies have not come down to us. strange thing-- as if a thing with which they had nothing to do.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12350"/><div sID="gen22569" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12350"/><hi type="bold">13. sacrifices of mine offerings--</hi>that is, which they offer to Me.<div eID="gen22569" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22570" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eat it--</hi>Their own carnal gratification is the object which they seek, not My honor.<div eID="gen22570" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22571" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">now--</hi>that is, "speedily."<div eID="gen22571" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22572" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall return to Egypt--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Hos.9.3">Ho 9:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.9.6">6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.11.11">11:11</reference>). The same threat as in <reference osisRef="Deut.28.68">De 28:68</reference>. They fled thither to escape from the Assyrians (compare as to Judah, Jr 42:1-44:30), when these latter had overthrown their nation. But see on <reference osisRef="Hos.9.3">Ho 9:3</reference>. <div eID="gen22572" type="x-p"/>

Maker--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Deut.32.18">De 32:18</reference>).<div eID="gen22573" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22574" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">temples--</hi>to idols.<div eID="gen22574" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22575" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Judah ... fenced cities--</hi>Judah, though less idolatrous than Israel, betrayed lack of faith in Jehovah by trusting more to its fenced cities than to Him; instead of making peace with God, Judah multiplied human defenses (<reference osisRef="Isa.22.8">Is 22:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.5.17">Jr 5:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.5.10">Mi 5:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.5.11">11</reference>).<div eID="gen22575" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22576" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will send ... fire upon ... cities--</hi>Sennacherib burned all Judah's fenced cities except Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.18.13">2Ki 18:13</reference>).<div eID="gen22576" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22577" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">palaces thereof--</hi>namely, of the land. entries.content_plain: 14. forgotten ... Maker-- ( De 32:18 ). temples-- to idols. I will send ... fire upon ... cities-- Sennacherib burned all Judah's fenced cities except Jerusalem ( 2Ki 18:13 ). palaces thereof-- namely, of the land. Compare as to Jerusalem, Jr 17:27 .
